title: Rigveda 9.54: To Soma
source: Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 (undated (catalogued with Penn's 18th-19th c. Vedic manuscripts)), OPenn, Public Domain Mark + Aufrecht's accented text (GRETIL) + Griffith's English (VedaWeb)
description: Rigveda 9.54: To Soma: Sanskrit text and Griffith's English, each verse linked to the page of an undated Rigveda manuscript (Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41) that carries it.
introduction:
Rigveda 9.54 is a hymn of 4 verses addressed to Soma. It stands in book (maṇḍala) 9, the hymns to Soma Pavamāna. The Rigveda is the oldest collection of Sanskrit hymns, composed in the second half of the second millennium BCE and handed down orally for many centuries before it was written down.

The manuscript shown is Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 (University of Pennsylvania), an undated paper manuscript of the padapāṭha (the word-by-word recitation text, in which every word is written separately and compounds are split) of the whole Ṛgveda in Devanāgarī, 884 leaves in fascicles, 7-9 lines to the page, accents in red; this hymn stands on fol. 687r-687v. Each section below gives the verses that end on one page; the page boundaries were read on the images (the opening words of every page), not counted out. Where the manuscript is a padapāṭha (the word-by-word recitation text), the section shows Aufrecht's continuous (saṃhitā) text first and, as the edition text, the padapāṭha of the same verses, which is the form written on the page.
translator_notes: Sanskrit: Aufrecht's edition (1877) with the Vedic accents, as entered by van Nooten and Holland (GRETIL).

English: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Rigveda (1889-1892; 2nd ed. 1896-1897), from the VedaWeb digital text; OCR slips in that text were corrected against the printed 2nd edition (data/sources/rigveda/griffith_errata.json).
Padapāṭha (edition text): Sansknet e-text via GRETIL (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0).

translation.original_ref: RV 9.54.1-3 (aṣṭaka 7, adhyāya 1, varga 11); Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 fol. 687r
translation.original_text:
1a̱sya pra̱tnām anu̱ dyuta̍ṁ śu̱kraṁ du̍duhre̱ ahra̍yaḥ | paya̍ḥ sahasra̱sām ṛṣi̍m ||
2a̱yaṁ sūrya̍ ivopa̱dṛg a̱yaṁ sarā̍ṁsi dhāvati | sa̱pta pra̱vata̱ ā diva̍m ||
3a̱yaṁ viśvā̍ni tiṣṭhati punā̱no bhuva̍no̱pari̍ | somo̍ de̱vo na sūrya̍ḥ ||
translation.text:
1AFTER his ancient splendour, they, the bold, have drawn the bright milk from The Sage who wins a thousand gifts.
2In aspect he is like the Sun; he runneth forward to the lakes, Seven currents flowing through the sky.
3He, shining in his splendour, stands high over all things that exist- Soma, a God as Sûrya is.
translation.scan_note: Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41, fol. 687r (numbered 4r by the scribe) (OPenn image 687, lower leaf). Checked on the image: the Rigveda text on this page begins in RV 9.52.3 ‹-itivadha-sno īṅkhaya›. The next page with Rigveda text, fol. 687v (numbered 4v by the scribe), begins in RV 9.54.4 ‹iti indra-yuḥ›. Verses 9.54.1-3 end on this page.
translation.edition_text:
1asya | pratnām | anu | dyutam | śukram | duduhre | ahrayaḥ | payaḥ | sahasra-sām | ṛṣim
2ayam | sūryaḥ-iva | upa-dṛk | ayam | sarāṃsi | dhāvati | sapta | pra-vataḥ | ā | divam
3ayam | viśvāni | tiṣṭhati | punānaḥ | bhuvanā | upari | somaḥ | divaḥ | na | sūryaḥ

translation.original_ref: RV 9.54.4 (aṣṭaka 7, adhyāya 1, varga 11); Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 fol. 687v
translation.original_text: <sup>4</sup>pari̍ ṇo de̱vavī̍taye̱ vājā̍m̐ arṣasi̱ goma̍taḥ | pu̱nā̱na i̍ndav indra̱yuḥ ||
translation.text: <sup>4</sup>Thou, Indu, in thy brilliancy, pourest on us, as Indra's Friend, Wealth from the kine to feast the Gods.
translation.scan_note: Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41, fol. 687v (numbered 4v by the scribe) (OPenn image 688, upper leaf). Checked on the image: the Rigveda text on this page begins in RV 9.54.4 ‹iti indra-yuḥ›. The next page with Rigveda text, fol. 688r (numbered 5r by the scribe), begins in RV 9.57.2 ‹cakṣāṇaḥ arṣati hariḥ tuñjānaḥ›. Verse 9.54.4 ends on this page; 9.54.4 begins on fol. 687r (numbered 4r by the scribe).
